items.title: What Changed In Dell's Story?
items.summary: Dell Technologies' (DELL) management no longer leads its earnings calls with the topic it stressed two years ago. That topic has not disappeared. Management still talks about it. The business behind it still brought in $51.0 billion, about 45% of Dell's revenue, in fiscal 2026. So it matters to you. What did Dell's management use to lead with.

items.title: Lenovo's Global Footprint Strengthens Its Growth Resilience
items.summary: LNVGY's global footprint across 180 markets and diversified revenue mix bolster resilience as fiscal 2026 revenues rise 20% to $83.1 billion.

items.title: Tech Exec Says China Is About to Burst the Memory Chip Pricing Bubble
items.summary: Acer's chairman just accused the world's biggest memory chip suppliers of using public shortage forecasts as a covert pricing signal, and he named a specific date when the whole story falls apart.

items.title: UBS Sees PC Sales Shrinking Again in 2027. Dell and HP Investors Aren’t Happy
items.summary: UBS just flipped its 2027 PC outlook from growth to decline, and the fallout hit Dell harder than HP even though HP has far more to lose. The reason comes down to what each stock had already priced in.

items.title: 2 Profitable Stocks to Target This Week and 1 That Underwhelm
items.summary: While profitability is essential, it doesn’t guarantee long-term success. Some companies that rest on their margins will lose ground as competition intensifies — as Jeff Bezos said, “Your margin is my opportunity”.

items.title: Why Is American Tower (AMT) Adding A New Board Voice On Talent And Governance?
items.summary: American Tower (NYSE:AMT) appointed Kristen M. Ludgate to its Board of Directors and its Compensation and Human Capital Committee. Ludgate previously served as Chief People Officer at HP Inc. and held senior leadership roles at 3M. She also brings board experience from companies in the banking and technology sectors. items.title: Can Dell's Margins Catch Up With Its Stock?
items.summary: Dell Technologies (DELL) stock has returned 341% over the past twelve months, the best record among the six companies in its peer group. Its revenue growth also ranks first. Its operating margin ranks only fourth, and that gap is what a buyer today has to judge. Behind the growth is demand for its servers that has outrun its own supply.
